questions.q: A ____ classroom is the changing face of learning.
questions.explanation: The digital classroom, using technology and online tools, reflects how learning is changing; closed or passive classrooms are what it moves away from.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a feature of e-learning?
questions.explanation: E-learning is learner-centred, offering accessibility, personalization and wider access (social justice). Teacher-centeredness is not one of its features.

questions.q: Which of the following is a synonym of e-learning?
questions.explanation: E-learning overlaps with audio-visual, multimedia and distance learning but is not synonymous with any of them; each is a distinct concept, so 'none of the above' is correct.

questions.q: In ____ e-learning course, the content is simple and comprises text, images, audio, powerpoint presentation and text questions.
questions.explanation: Text-driven e-learning courses are simple, made up of text, images, audio, presentations and test questions. Interactive and simulation-based courses add more engagement and realistic practice.

questions.q: Recent thinking in cognitive psychology places the ____ firmly at the center of the learning experience.
questions.explanation: Cognitive psychology views learning as the learner's own active mental construction, so the individual learner is placed at the centre of the learning experience.

questions.q: Which of the following is true?
questions.explanation: Learning depends on self-awareness (metacognition), is social (shaped by interaction with others) and is goal-oriented, so all the statements are true.

questions.q: Learners may multitask when engaging in an online course, which could be resulting in ____.
questions.explanation: Multitasking splits attention across activities, which shortens attention spans and impairs encoding. It does not produce hyperfocus or better retrieval.

questions.q: The brain can process ____ visual cues per hour!
questions.explanation: The lecture cites the commonly quoted figure that the brain can process about 36,000 visual cues per hour, used to argue for visual design in online courses.

questions.q: Our brain has approximately ____ neurons that send information to one another.
questions.explanation: The human brain contains roughly 85-86 billion neurons that communicate with one another through synapses.

questions.q: ____ is referring to learners' automatic performance on specific procedures with predetermined steps to be followed.
questions.explanation: The key treats chaining as learners' automatic performance of a fixed sequence of predetermined steps, where each step cues the next.
questions.flag: Ambiguous: the description ('automatic performance on specific procedures with predetermined steps') reads most naturally as automatization (option B); chaining is linking steps into a sequence. Key keeps chaining, presumably as worded in the lecture.
